summary_of_pdf: This document is an RPost registered email receipt serving as verifiable, court-admissible proof of delivery and read-receipt for a formal legal notice sent to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and City of Houston officials. The underlying communication asserts provisional patent rights under 35 U.S.C. § 154(d) concerning 'Aviation Infrastructure and RF De-anonymization,' unilaterally grants a federal license, and demands due diligence. The transmission includes attachments detailing a USPTO patent application portfolio, EPO defensive publications, and a DOJ-related memorandum.
attorneys_comments: The RPost receipt provides robust evidentiary proof of actual notice to key FAA and municipal stakeholders, satisfying the stringent actual notice requirements for provisional damages under 35 U.S.C. § 154(d). Tactically, the unilateral 'Federal License Grant' appears to be a calculated maneuver to force the government's use into a 28 U.S.C. § 1498(a) posture, thereby shielding municipal actors from direct infringement injunctions while preserving a damages claim in the Court of Federal Claims. A notable weakness is the reliance on pending applications rather than issued patents, precluding immediate injunctive relief. Furthermore, the inclusion of the 'DOJ Alumni Network' attachment introduces extraneous elements that could dilute the substantive patent claims. Procedurally, this instrument establishes a firm, indisputable timeline for willful infringement or reasonable royalty calculations post-publication.
recommended_next_steps: 1. Docket the date of actual notice (April 10, 2026) for future damages calculations under 35 U.S.C. § 154(d). 2. Monitor the referenced USPTO applications for allowance and issuance to perfect the right to initiate litigation. 3. Prepare a defensive memorandum assessing whether the City of Houston's use of the accused RF infrastructure falls under the 28 U.S.C. § 1498(a) federal government authorization and consent doctrine. 4. Conduct a preliminary infringement analysis of the attached patent portfolio against current FAA/IAH RF de-anonymization deployments.
